identity_rule: Lower levels may add detail but must preserve the parent identity and must not silently redefine an accepted higher-level element.

levels.name: generic context model
entry: pinned architecture, explainer, scenario, or system description
defined target, user goal, scope, and intended review decision
work: keep the capability as a black box where useful
identify users, affected people, principals, main external entities, minimum directional flows, and first authority or trust boundaries
record detail deliberately deferred to L1, L2, or implementation mapping
exit: source coverage, assumptions, and unresolved questions

levels.name: specification and API-surface model
entry: pinned WebIDL or equivalent public API and normative state definitions
work: inventory interfaces, operations, attributes, dictionaries, callbacks, enums, typedefs, relevant return types, exposure gates, normative state, and lifecycle relationships
map behaviorally meaningful methods to stable logical processes
keep dictionaries as typed data contracts rather than drawing every dictionary as a process
exit: webidl-api-surface-inventory/v1 or an equivalent API-surface artifact
L1 model and DFD refinement with stable L0 parent links
explicit gates, state, directional flows, assumptions, and deferred algorithm detail

levels.name: normative algorithm child analysis
entry: one selected L1 operation with a stable parent process identifier
pinned WebIDL and complete numbered normative procedure
work: begin with Phase 0 WebIDL exposure and argument conversion before the first numbered step
preserve conversion order, getters, proxies, iterators, string conversion, callback validation, promise behavior, and conversion failures or side effects
group numbered steps into ordered review-useful subprocesses without dropping or reordering behavior
record executor, input and state, state transition, delegated algorithm, security property, precondition, exception, failure behavior, residual or non-guarantee, DFD mapping, and test decision
exit: stable link to the L1 parent and child-only process identifiers
separate evidence, implementation mapping, review judgment, open questions, and test decisions

implementation_mapping.rule: Renderer state, browser-side registries, IPC, dispatch, feature flags, and implementation stores may be mapped only after the specification model is stable.

completion_rule: A schema-valid artifact is not methodologically complete by itself; the selected level must be sufficient for the current review decision and threat traceability.
